findings.evidence: Lines 60–69 replace `haarProb G` by `μ`; thereafter the proof uses only the two installed typeclasses and generic map/uniqueness APIs.
findings.fix: First prove right invariance for an arbitrary measure `μ` with `[μ.IsHaarMeasure] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]`, then derive this instance for `haarProb`.
findings.issue: `isMulRightInvariant_haarProb` uses only `μ.IsHaarMeasure` and `IsProbabilityMeasure μ`, so specializing the full uniqueness proof to `haarProb` loses the reusable general theorem.

findings.evidence: Lines 74–86 use no property of the normalization formula: only `μ.IsHaarMeasure`, `IsProbabilityMeasure μ`, right invariance, and generic inversion/map uniqueness.
findings.fix: Generalize the proof to arbitrary `μ` with Haar/probability hypotheses (using the generalized right-invariance result), then obtain the `haarProb` instance as a corollary.
findings.issue: `isInvInvariant_haarProb` is likewise a special-case proof of inversion invariance for any probability Haar measure that is right-invariant.

summary: The right- and inversion-invariance arguments are unnecessarily specialized to `haarProb`; their proofs establish the natural result for every probability Haar measure.
